about: Traceability of the financial methods (docs/financial-methods.md, sections 1 to 12) to the tests that prove them (QG-03.4). Each requirement is a rule or an edge case; `tests` are pytest functions (file::function, under backend/); `covers` are the public functions of the financial modules that implement it. backend/tests/test_financial_matrix.py fails if a listed test does not exist, if a section has no requirement, or if a public function of a financial module is covered by no requirement. docs/financial-test-matrix.md is generated from this file by scripts/test_matrix.py.

requirements.text: Amounts are plain decimal strings; JSON numbers, exponents, signs, spaces and over-long values are refused
ISO 4217 minor units (JPY 0, KWD 3, default 2)
Rounding is half-up: ties go away from zero, including negatives
Amounts that must be enough are rounded up (ADR-0006 exception 1), never to a negative zero
Largest-remainder shares add up to exactly 100.00, ties to the earlier part, undefined for a non-positive total or negative parts
A trade's gross is quantity x price, rounded half-up; a given gross must agree within one minor unit
Each type has its required and forbidden fields; only a valuation adjustment can be negative; amounts use the currency's minor units; FX rate required for foreign postings
A reversed entry and its reversal are left out as if never posted; entries order by date, creation, id
Weighted average cost: buys add (gross+fees+taxes) x fx, sales remove average x quantity, realised = proceeds - cost removed
Income and expenses per asset at the posting's rate; entries without an asset are ignored
A sale beyond the units held on its date is refused; no units means no cost; cost is conserved
Cash effect of every transaction type
Totals reconcile: value = positions + cash; breakdown adds up; unrealised, realised and net contributions agree with an independent computation
Edge cases: closed positions not valued, reversed entries ignored, negative cash shown as is, published figures round half-up
Consolidation converts each portfolio at the latest rate and reconciles; unconvertible portfolios are reported
Freshness is the oldest input; completeness; amounts without a rate are left out and reported

A position is valued from the latest market price (quantity x price, exact), falling back to the latest manual valuation; a newer manual valuation beats an older price, a tie goes to the price, manually valued assets ignore prices, nothing known is unpriced; stale prices are used and flagged, never hidden
Newest rate at or before the moment wins; a historical date uses that day's end; rates older than 7 days are unusable
The opposite pair is inverted only without a direct rate; ties by retrieval then provider; non-positive rates ignored
Conversion keeps every digit until the output, then rounds half-up; the same currency is 1
A currency without a usable rate is left out and reported, never converted at a guess

Without either direction of a pair, the rate goes through the pivot: the product of the legs, as old as the older leg, stale if either is, with its path; a stored pair wins; ledger postings never cross
Allocation by asset class, currency, country and sector; cash and missing values in their own slices; all dimensions add up to the same total
Concentration: HHI, effective positions, top-1/3/5 shares and the largest position
Edge cases: negative cash leaves shares undefined; nothing to allocate; zero-valued positions; deterministic order
External flows: deposits and transfers in, withdrawals and transfers out, at posting rates; reversals and zero flows excluded
Profit and simple return; undefined when nothing was put in
CAGR: actual/365, only for at least a year, total loss is -100%
XIRR: published Excel example, exact cases, two roots, and every failure state; NPV zero at the rate; independent of scale and calendar shift; agrees with Newton at 80 digits
Time-weighted return handles external flows, emptied portfolios and undefined periods; annualised only from a year; dates must increase
Assumed deposits cover a currency's shortfall at the posting's date and rate, for performance and risk only, reported separately
Performance of a real ledger reconciles: gain = realised + unrealised + income - expenses; recorded deposits are not assumed again; another user's portfolio is not found
Trailing twelve months, with the leap-day rule; future payments excluded
Calendar months and years; periods cross the year boundary; periods add up
Totals at each payment's rate: gross, fees, taxes and net; monthly and yearly passive income
Yields on gross: current, on cost and portfolio; undefined for a non-positive base
Income events follow the ledger (posting, reversal, replay) and are isolated per portfolio and user
Compound forecast: nominal return compounded at the chosen frequency, fees as a drag, end-of-period contributions, yearly escalation, inflation-adjusted values
Edge cases: zero rate, negative rate, 50-year horizon, largest inputs, domain edges and refusals
Properties: contributions + growth = value; monotone in return, fee, contributions and horizon; inflation lowers only the real value; deterministic; no float or LLM
Scenarios change only the return
Required contribution (closed form, rounded up): nominal and real targets, already reached, zero rate, negative target refused, never short of the target
Month horizons: value after N months, months to reach a target, required contribution by a date, including no contribution date before the horizon
The forecast API enforces the published limits, echoes assumptions, returns nominal and real series, states the not-guaranteed notice, and shares its limits with the mobile calculator
Whole months between dates and adding months (month-end clamping, negative spans)

Progress, gap, status, required contribution and estimated completion under stated assumptions: on track, behind, reached, overdue, under a month left, today's-money targets, scenario order, negative value, never reached, minor units
Goals through the API: funding from one or all portfolios, summary counts, estimates labelled, ownership enforced
Net worth = assets - liabilities in one currency; each liability rounded first so the figures reconcile exactly; negative net worth shown
FX provenance, unconverted currencies and freshness are reported; another currency; isolation between users
History dates (daily, weekly, month-end, limits) and end-of-day values rebuilt from the ledger, valuations and historical FX
Period returns by Modified Dietz (weights, several flows, daily unchanged); empty and undefined periods
Volatility: sample standard deviation annualised, against the statistics module and the exact variance
Maximum drawdown on the linked index with peak, trough and recovery; earliest of equal falls; no fall
Time-weighted return of a series by linking, annualised only from a year
Explicit statuses, never partial figures: ok, insufficient data (fewer than 12 returns), incomplete data, undefined period
Risk of a real portfolio: a deposit is not a return; a mid-month deposit is weighted by its days; ranges are checked; ownership enforced
Analytics endpoints publish the figures at the documented rounding, behind authentication and per-user authorisation
The analytics cache never serves another user's data and is invalidated by any successful write
The workbook vectors computed by the independent oracle agree with the application
Each concentration measure (holding, asset class, sector, country) is graded at its thresholds; sector and country use known values only and report an unknown share
Foreign-currency exposure is the share not in the base currency, graded at its thresholds
Liquidity is the accessible share from stated class liquidity, flagged when small; every asset class has a stated liquidity
Volatility and drawdown come from the risk measures and are not assessed, with the reason, without enough history
Income dependence is the largest payer's share of trailing gross income; no income is not assessed
Goal alignment: overdue goals are high, goals behind medium, reached goals are not a concern
Incomplete data is reported; an empty or negative portfolio is not assessed
A scenario cap keeps the total and the proportions of the rest, and is never a trade
The diagnosis is deterministic: every check in a fixed order, the same result whatever the input order, ties resolved by id
Weekly sampling keeps the last close of each ISO week; price features reuse the risk maths over the trailing year
A feature that cannot be measured is missing with its reason: short history, no prices, manual valuation, no expense ratio, unknown liquidity; stale closes are flagged
Each factor's transform at its boundaries, clamped to 0-100
The score is the weighted mean of measured factors and equals the sum of the contributions; cost does not apply to non-funds
Missing data lowers coverage and confidence; below 50% coverage there is no score; stale prices keep confidence below high
Weights name every factor, are not negative and add up to 1; settings refuse others
A hypothetical amount is added as new money: a new holding or a larger one, the total grows by the amount, the original is unchanged
Before and after measures (instrument share, largest holding, effective positions, class share, foreign currency, accessible share) use the allocation maths

Verdict: not suitable when ineligible or below the minimum (converted at the stored rate); caution when the minimum cannot be checked, a Doctor check worsens to medium or high, or the instrument would exceed the medium holding threshold; fits otherwise
Simple and exponential moving averages: SMA is the plain mean of the last n values; EMA uses alpha = 2/(n+1) seeded with the SMA of the first n values; both first defined at index n-1
MACD line = EMA(fast) - EMA(slow); signal = EMA of the MACD line seeded with its first signal-period values; histogram = line - signal; fast must be shorter than slow
RSI with Wilder smoothing seeded with the mean of the first n gains and losses; 100 with gains and no losses, undefined (None) with neither; matches the published worked example
Stochastic %K over the k-bar range (None for a flat range), smoothed by an SMA, and %D as the SMA of %K; bounded to 0..100
Rate of change in percent against the value n bars earlier; None when that value is zero
True range uses the gap to the previous close; ATR is its Wilder average seeded with the mean of the first n true ranges
ADX: Wilder-smoothed directional movement and true range, +DI and -DI (0 for a flat range), DX and its Wilder average seeded with the mean of the first n DX values
Bollinger Bands: SMA middle, bands at k population standard deviations, bandwidth (upper - lower) / middle
Indicators are Decimal-only and look only backwards: value i computed on bars 0..i equals value i on all bars; scale and shift properties hold
Session calendar: trading days of 24 hours from 17:00 New York, named after the day they end on; the week runs Sunday 17:00 to Friday 17:00 New York; daylight saving moves the open in UTC only
Timeframe boundaries from the calendar (intraday from the day open, 1D, 1W, 1M by trading date) and the expected one-minute count of a full period (weekdays only for a month)
Aggregation: first open, extremes, last close, summed volume; missing minutes flagged partial, empty periods absent, closed-market candles ignored, forming periods marked, never filled
Swing points: strictly beyond the left bars and at least as far as the right bars, confirmed only after the right bars (no look-ahead)
Support and resistance: swings grouped within a tolerance into levels with touch counts; role relative to the price; breakouts are decisive closes beyond a level after it was established
Trendlines through the last two swings of a kind, with validity since the second point; channels as the parallel through the furthest opposite extreme

Candlestick rules with stated thresholds and trend context: doji, marubozu, hammer, hanging man, shooting star, inverted hammer, engulfing, harami, inside bar, morning and evening star, three soldiers and crows; every hit cites its candles
Price action: range consolidation against an ATR multiple (each run once) and breakout-and-retest within a window

The analysis API returns exactly the library values (rounded half-up to 8 places) on stored provider candles, prefers provider candles of the requested timeframe, and reports partial and truncated data

Setup rules are named and versioned, read only closed bars, and return illustrative levels with the stop (invalidation) and target on the correct sides of the entry; a setup whose level falls on the wrong side is not reported
Reversal, range, momentum and mean-reversion rules with their stated thresholds and targets
Opportunity score = 100 x clip(sum of weight x component, 0, 1); components in [0, 1]; macro-event risk is a penalty; positive weights sum to 1 (validated); half-up to 0.1
Market condition (priority: high volatility, trending, momentum strengthening, consolidating, mixed) and risk level (volatility, spread and event points)

Every candidate lists all ten factors with value, weight and contribution, and the factors give the score; stale data is excluded; event windows (x 0.5) and missing quotes (x 0.75) demote, each with its reason; an uncalibrated forecast contributes nothing
Candidates are research candidates: no text gives advice, a trade instruction or a guarantee

The pip value is never a constant: pip size is 10^pip_location, the pip value per lot in the quote currency is contract size x pip size, and in the account currency it is converted at a stored rate (exactly 1 only when the quote currency is the account currency), including JPY and cross pairs

The conversion rate comes from stored quotes with its path, time and data types: the same currency, a direct pair, its inverse, or a cross through USD, kept as an exact fraction; a missing rate is refused, never assumed; stale and less liquid (indicative) rates are marked

The size is the largest multiple of the lot step whose planned loss at the stop, including spread, slippage and commission for entry and exit, does not exceed balance x risk percent; below the minimum size nothing is sized and above the maximum the size is capped, each with a warning; an independent exact oracle agrees

Loss and profit before and after costs, risk/reward before and after costs, margin (notional x margin rate), position leverage (notional / balance), the specification's maximum leverage, margin use, account impact and signed exposure per currency, each rounded as stated

Warnings for the risk, leverage and margin-use limits, insufficient margin, a non-tradable or stale conversion rate, an unknown spread, unreviewed specifications and less liquid pairs; disclosures always state that stops can slip or gap and that leverage amplifies losses, and no text promises an outcome

Contract specifications are versioned and reviewed: a new version supersedes the old, a changed value needs a new version, one version is active per pair, a review names its reviewer, and a provider's differing values are reported, not applied

The clock: a decision made at a bar's close fills at the next bar's open; a decision on the last bar is not filled; one position at a time; later bars never change an earlier trade; decisions see only copies of the closed bars

Fills and exits: half the spread and the slippage against the position on every fill and commission per side; the size from the risk engine stays within the risk; exits in the stated order (gap through the stop at the open, gap through the target, stop before target within one bar, target, holding limit, end); entries skipped after a gap past a level or below the minimum size

Metrics net of costs: total return, maximum drawdown, win rate, profit factor, average trade, expectancy in R, longest losing streak, exposure, Sharpe and Sortino annualised by the stated bars per year, with the empty and no-loss cases

Walk-forward: parameters chosen on window k by in-sample net return are tested once on window k + 1; windows never overlap and no position crosses an edge; out-of-sample windows are compounded; stability is reported
Benchmarks on the same out-of-sample bars (no trade, buy and hold with costs, seeded random entry) and cost sensitivity that only raises costs, never removes them

Look-ahead and reproducibility: the leakage audit fails a deliberately leaky strategy and passes the real rules; the same bars, parameters, seed and code give the same report hash; a rule's out-of-sample history counts in the opportunity score only from 30 trades, as clip(profit factor - 1), labelled with its data type

Paper fills are at the stored bid or ask, never the mid: a market buy at ask + slippage, a market sell at bid - slippage, a limit at its price once the quote reaches it; an order needs a fresh, non-suspect quote

Stops and targets are triggered by the quotes in time order: a stop fills as a market order at the triggering quote with slippage (a gap fills beyond the stop), a target at its price; the first trigger wins

Sizes are multiples of the lot step within the specification's limits; the stop and target sit on the losing and winning sides of the entry; commission per lot per side; an order beyond the free paper margin is refused and limits give warnings

Realised P/L is earned in the quote currency and converted into the account currency at the rates of the closing quote's time; costs paid against the mid and commissions are reported; margin and equity follow

Paper analytics over closed positions: net P/L, win rate, profit factor, average, best and worst, costs, maximum drawdown of the closed balance, return on the starting balance, losing streak, by strategy tag and by pair; labelled as the paper series
Paper money stays apart: separate tables never read by real-money modules, net worth unchanged by paper trades, PAPER TRADING on every response, and every paper resource hidden from other users
